background.definition: Gilbert’s disease is a hereditary disorder characterized by isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in the absence of underlying liver disease or hemolysis. Bilirubin levels are usually 2 to 3 mg/dL and are rarely greater than 6 mg/dL.

list.listitem: Two percent to 10% of population.
Greater incidence among males and caucasians.
Patients with Gilbert’s who take protease inhibitors may experience increased elevations of bilirubin and jaundice.

Patients with Gilbert’s syndrome (UGT1A1 deficiency) are at significantly increased risk for severe toxicity (neutropenia and diarrhea) if treated with irinotecan (used for colorectal cancer) or sacituzumab govitecan.
Inherited
Mutations in the enzyme uridine diphosphate glucuronyltransferase (UGT1A1) lead to ineffective conjugation of bilirubin.
Mainly a diagnosis of exclusion with the finding of elevated unconjugated bilirubin levels in the absence of liver disease. C
Rifampin provocation testing and caloric restriction of doubtful benefit (low specificity). C

Elevated alkaline phosphatase, ruq pain, abnormal imaging
Abdominal pain, fever, elevated alkaline phosphatase

list.listitem: Patients are asymptomatic or may have occasional, intermittent, and mild jaundice.
Any complaint other than occasional jaundice or any laboratory abnormality other than mild, unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia should prompt an investigation for a disease process other than Gilbert’s.
Gilbert’s is a diagnosis of exclusion.

Caloric restriction and administration of rifampin have been show to increase bilirubin levels in patients with Gilbert’s. However, because of the lack of uniformity in methods and low specificity, there is no useful clinical application for these tests.
Usually an incidental finding on laboratory testing, detected during adolescence or early adulthood.
Bilirubin levels usually 2 to 3 mg/dL and rarely greater than 6 mg/dL.
Order a Coomb’s test and a serum LDH to rule out hemolysis; serology to rule out viral hepatits; and AST, ALT, PT, and serum albumin to rule out other underlying liver disease.
If these are abnormal order appropriate further studies such as imaging to confirm the diagnosis.

PCR testing for the UGT1A1*28 mutation is available but usually unnecessary, and should be considered only when the diagnosis is uncertain, other causes cannot be excluded by routine labs, or before starting irinotecan.
No relevant clinical decision rules found.
Take a thorough history to rule out other causes of underlying liver disease, including thorough drug or alcohol history.
Order a Coomb’s test and a serum LDH to rule out hemolysis; serology to rule out viral hepatits; and AST, ALT, PT, and serum albumin to rule out other underlying liver disease.
No treatment required; this is a benign condition. C
Benign disorder with no increase in morbidity or mortality. B

Multiple large cohort studies suggest that patients with Gilbert’s syndrome have lower rates of CAD, atherosclerosis, and all-cause mortality, likely because mildly elevated bilirubin acts as an endogenous antioxidant that reduces oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation.
Patients may have an increased risk of developing gallstones (specifically pigment stones) due to increased excretion of unconjugated bilirubin.
